clue.text: 20 serving girls inside a thingummy

indicators.note: inside says the servicewomen sit within the other piece

parts.note: 20 points to the clue at 20 across, 'a very small quantity', for which whit is a synonym
the ATS, the Auxiliary Territorial Service, was the women's branch of the British Army

explanation.surface: Twenty waitresses crammed into some unnamed gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' is a cross-reference to another clue's definition, not a number of waitresses; 'serving girls' recalls the wartime women's army service.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingummy and a whatsit are both colloquial names for an object whose proper name escapes the speaker.

clue.text: Two-step in dancing academy

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters are moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A ballroom dance performed at a stage school.
explanation.walkthrough: West Point is the United States Military Academy in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: West Point is home to the US Military Academy, which trains army officers.

clue.text: In Shangri-La they were smaller after a time

indicators.note: after says the word for smaller follows the word for a time

parts.note: an age is a period of time
less means smaller in amount

explanation.surface: In the fabled valley, people shrank as time went by.
explanation.walkthrough: In James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, the inhabitants of Shangri-La do not grow old.
explanation.definitionFit: People in Shangri-La never grew old, so they were timeless, immune to the years.

clue.text: Tin god first going up Alabama waterway

indicators.note: first says the god comes before the tin
in a down clue, going up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: Zeus is the king of the Greek gods
a can is a tin container
AL is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Alabama

explanation.surface: A false idol climbing up through an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin god' looks like one phrase, a petty tyrant, but its two words work separately; 'first' moves the god ahead of the tin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suez Canal is an artificial channel linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.

clue.text: Mouth actor's words the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: an actor's part is the lines given to his role

explanation.surface: Lip-synching a performer's lines incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth' looks like a verb, to mouth words, but it is the noun, slang for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.

clue.text: Kind of crossing made by Drake's ship originally

explanation.surface: A type of road crossing devised by the famous Elizabethan sea captain's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: A PELICAN crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with lights the walker controls; Sir Francis Drake's Golden Hind set out under this name before being renamed.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a signal-controlled pedestrian crossing in Britain; the other is the original name of the ship Drake sailed round the world.

clue.text: The pursuit of knowledge brings boy round girl

parts.note: Phil is a boy's name
O is a round shape
Sophy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Studying leads a lad to put his arm round a lass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a containment signal, but it is simply the round letter O, placed between the two names.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek roots mean love of wisdom, and philosophy is the study of knowledge and reality.

clue.text: A great number not working after eating this?

definitions.text: A great number not working after eating this?

parts.note: a lot is a great number
U/S, unserviceable, means out of action

explanation.surface: Many people became idle after eating this plant.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer's Odyssey the lotus-eaters lose all wish to work or go home after eating the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the lotus fruit induced dreamy laziness in those who ate it.

clue.text: Ship's barber

explanation.surface: A sailor's hairdresser.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipper is a fast sailing ship; a barber clips hair, so he is one who clips.

clue.text: It's simple saying "No" to a child

indicators.note: saying signals the words are spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: no is nay and a child is a kid, put together

explanation.surface: Refusing a youngster is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked can mean plain or unadorned, as in the naked truth.

clue.text: Kid had a swing, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: to have a swing is to sway, so had a swing gives swayed

explanation.surface: A child played on a swing, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the soft leather made from a young goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is fine leather from young goats, and suede is leather with a napped finish, so both name soft leathers.

clue.text: A doorstep is more than one could reasonably expect

definitions.text: more than one could reasonably expect

explanation.surface: A visitor at the door is demanding too much.
explanation.walkthrough: A doorstep is British slang for a very thick slice of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstep sandwich is chunky bread; and the idiom for an unreasonable demand is that it is excessive or unfair.

clue.text: Quietly communicate with advocate

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to reach someone is to get in touch or communicate with them

explanation.surface: Have a soft word with your lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a cause is to urge or recommend it publicly, as a sermon urges virtue.

clue.text: Disposing of pigs, does spread tales

indicators.note: disposing in its sense of arranging or setting out tells us to rearrange the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A farmer selling off his swine while the female deer chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposing of' reads as getting rid of, but here it means arranging: the letters of PIGS and DOES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread tales about people is to tattle or talk idly about their affairs.

clue.text: Life-guard — he's lost pounds — ruined — bust

indicators.note: ruined says the letters are wrecked into a new order
lost says the pounds letter is taken out

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra
he's reads as he, the 's merely linking

explanation.surface: A lifeguard has slimmed down, but his chest has suffered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes L from LIFEGUARD; 'ruined' rearranges IFEGUARD plus HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's figurehead is often a carved bust of a person on the prow.

clue.text: Children's writer almost turned into a playwright

indicators.note: turned means the shortened name is read backwards
almost means the writer's name loses its final letter

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children and other children's books

explanation.surface: An author of books for children nearly became a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts NESBIT to NESBI and 'turned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, the Norwegian author of A Doll's House, is a famous dramatist.

clue.text: Engine smooth? Sounds rough

parts.note: to iron clothes is to smooth them

indicators.note: sounds says the word for rough is heard and spelt differently

parts.note: a rough voice is hoarse

explanation.surface: Is the motor running smoothly? It sounds rough.
explanation.walkthrough: An iron horse is an old name for a railway locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse is a nineteenth-century nickname for the steam locomotive, the railway engine.

clue.text: Turn in popular show — they receive half a laugh

parts.note: a hit is a popular show

indicators.note: receive says the half laugh goes inside they
half means only the first half of the laugh is used

parts.note: ha-ha is a laugh

explanation.surface: A turn in a successful show gets a chuckle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like a performer's act, but 'turn in' means go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the hay is an idiom for going to bed, as is turn in.

clue.text: Rare spirit, possibly fiery

explanation.surface: An unusual liquor, perhaps one that burns.
explanation.definitionFit: An elemental is a nature spirit; and fire is one of the classical elements, so fiery may be described thus.

clue.text: Stars help tough to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Celebrities help a hard man turn his life around.
explanation.walkthrough: THE PLOUGH is the British name for the constellation Americans call the Big Dipper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plough is a group of seven bright stars in Ursa Major, a well-known asterism.

clue.text: Oriental festival, originally Nipponese

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A celebration that began in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things from the East.

clue.text: Manage to find a very small quantity

explanation.surface: Succeed in locating a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace something lost is to track it down; a trace is also a minute amount, as in traces of poison.

clue.text: Charge a sailor for the "Listener"

indicators.note: for the listener means as heard, the words sounding like another

parts.note: a salt, an old salt, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Accusing a seaman on behalf of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a BBC magazine, so 'Listener' looks like a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge an enemy is to rush at and attack them.

clue.text: Jack's dish? No right to it — he's not here.

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, an AB or able seaman; with the possessive it gives AB'S

indicators.note: no in front of right says that letter is taken away

parts.note: an entree is a dish served at a meal

explanation.surface: A sailor is refused his plate of food, and he is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is the old slang for a sailor, as is AB; 'to it' merely links the deletion to the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is someone missing from a place where they are expected.

clue.text: Has picked some lavender

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone has gathered a bunch of a fragrant herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is an old name for spike lavender, a fragrant plant of the mint family.

clue.text: In EEC, strangely, one's part of a family…

indicators.note: strangely means the letters are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: Inside the European Economic Community, oddly, one is a member of a clan.
explanation.walkthrough: The EEC was the European Economic Community, forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a relative.

clue.text: Good number joining expedition

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
expedition in its older sense means speed or haste

explanation.surface: A fine number of people sign up for a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' looks like a journey but means promptness, as in 'expeditious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means virtuous and pure, the moral sense of good.

clue.text: …a group of countries that halves the restriction of trade

indicators.note: halves means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: a blockade cuts off a country's trade

explanation.surface: A league of nations that cuts embargoes in half.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of states acting together.

clue.text: Gradually assemble some food

parts.note: to piece something together is to assemble it
a meal is some food eaten at one sitting

explanation.surface: Slowly put together something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Done piecemeal means done bit by bit, a little at a time.

clue.text: Starts housekeeping accounts — unfortunately, not that frequent

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Keeping household books is unhappily not something done often.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt a place is to visit it often, as in a favourite haunt.

clue.text: Cunningly persuade minister to compete

parts.note: to con someone is to persuade them by trickery
to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: A slick talker coaxes a clergyman into entering a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks like a noun, a clergyman, but it is the verb to care for.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to strive or vie with rivals.

clue.text: Offer for sale a lot of old glass

parts.note: street sellers cry their wares, offering them for sale

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, the last letter dropped

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh

explanation.surface: Putting a batch of antique glassware up at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' cuts STALE to STAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal is fine, clear, high-quality glass.
